title: Suspicious sign-in alert
symptom: An alert shows a sign-in to a user's account from another country
user_description: I got an email saying someone signed in to my account from another country last night. I was at home asleep. Is that real?

options.text: Ignore it because MFA is on
options.why: MFA can be tricked or bypassed. A strange sign-in still needs checking.

options.text: Email her a link to confirm her password
options.why: This looks exactly like phishing and teaches people to trust such links.

options.text: Wait and see if a second alert comes
options.why: An attacker could be reading mail or sending phishing right now.

options.text: Phone her on a number you already have and ask if it was her (travel, VPN?). If not: reset the password, revoke sessions, check MFA methods and mail rules, then escalate
options.why: Confirming through a trusted channel avoids being fooled. If it was not her, locking the attacker out quickly matters most.

hints: How can you check the alert is real, safely?
Is there an innocent reason, like a VPN or travel?
What does an attacker often change after getting in?
real_world_tip: Tell her not to click links in the alert email itself. Check the sign-in in the admin portal directly.

escalation.team_why: Unknown sign-ins are security incidents. The security team checks what the attacker did and whether other accounts were targeted.

details.text: The time and location from the alert
details.why: Lets them find the sign-in in the logs.

details.text: Her confirmation that it was not her
details.why: Turns a possible alert into a confirmed incident.

details.text: What you have already done (password reset, sessions revoked, MFA checked)
details.why: Avoids repeated work and shows what is still to check.
Never share passwords, and you have already reset it.
